Rashi on Bekhorot 9b:10:1.hebrew: שפדיונו מותר - כגון הכא, שהכהן אוכל את השה בלא שום הקרבה, והוא אסור קודם פדיון. דהא פסולי המוקדשין, שאסורין בהנאה קודם פדיונן, הוי פדיונן נתפס בקדושתן ואסור:
Rashi on Bekhorot 9b:10:1.english: Whereby its redemption is permitted - Such as here, where the priest eats the lamb without any sacrifice, and it is forbidden prior to redemption. For behold, disqualified consecrated animals, which are forbidden for benefit prior to their redemption, their redemption [payment] assumes their sanctity and is forbidden.

Rashi on Bekhorot 9b:11:1.hebrew: שביעית - המוכר פירות שביעית, הדמים מותרין לעולם, והפירות עצמן מתבערין בשעת הביעור, כשכלה לחיה. וקס"ד דהאי מקשה, דפדיון שביעית מותר לעולם, ולא שמיעא ליה הא דאחרון אחרון נתפס:
Rashi on Bekhorot 9b:11:1.english: Sabbatical [produce] - [In the case of] one who sells produce of the Sabbatical Year, the money is permitted forever, and the produce itself must be removed at the time of removal, when [such produce] ceases for the wild beast. And it entered the mind of this questioner that the redemption [money] of Sabbatical [produce] is permitted forever, and he had not heard that [ruling] that the very last [item] is seized [by its sanctity].

Rashi on Bekhorot 9b:12:1.hebrew: אחרון אחרון - במס' סוכה (דף מ:): לקח בפירות שביעית בשר — אלו ואלו מתבערין בשעת הביעור. לקח בבשר יין — יצא בשר ונכנס יין; יין בשמן — יצא יין ונכנס שמן, ואחרון נתפס בשביעית להתבער. ופרי עצמו שגדל בשביעית, שבאו אלו מכחו, בכ"מ שהוא — אסור מן הביעור ואילך:
Rashi on Bekhorot 9b:12:1.english: The very last - In Tractate Sukkah (40b): [If] one purchased meat with Sabbatical produce, both these and those must be removed at the time of the removal. [If] he purchased wine with the meat, the meat exits and the wine enters; [if he purchased] oil with wine, the wine exits and the oil enters, and the last [item] is seized by [the sanctity of] the Sabbatical Year to be removed. And the produce itself that grew in the Sabbatical Year, through whose power these came, wherever it is, is forbidden from the [time of] removal and onward.

Rashi on Bekhorot 9b:13:1.hebrew: בשלך ושל אחרים - עובדי כוכבים. כגון בכור בהמה שיש בה שותפות לעובד כוכבים — אע"ג דמחייב ר' יהודה למיתב חצי דמיו לכהן — שרי בגיזה ועבודה, שאין קדושה לחצאין. אבל פטר חמור לא ממעט מהאי קרא, וכל כמה דלא ממעט לא שרינן ליה, דלא גרע מבכור בהמה טהורה; ולרבי שמעון ממעט ליה קרא:
Rashi on Bekhorot 9b:13:1.english: With yours and that of others - [Namely,] gentiles. For example, the firstborn of an animal in which there is partnership with a gentile — even though Rabbi Yehuda obligates [one] to give half its value to a priest — is permitted for shearing and work, as there is no partial sanctity. But the firstborn of a donkey is not excluded by this verse, and as long as it is not excluded, we do not permit it, for it is no less [strictly forbidden] than the firstborn of a kosher animal; and according to Rabbi Shimon, the verse excludes it.

Rashi on Bekhorot 9b:18:1.english: Granted, according to Rabbi Yehuda - For he expounds: “Your flock” — and not [an animal owned in] partnership with a gentile.

Rashi on Bekhorot 9b:18:2.hebrew: היינו דכתיב צאנך - דמשמע המיוחד לך, ולא כתב צאן סתמא. ושורך — אע"ג דמצי למיכתב בבכור שור, ומימעט נמי בכור אדם מיניה — אפי' הכי, אטו צאנך כתב שורך:
Rashi on Bekhorot 9b:18:2.english: This is why “your flock” is written - As it implies that which is uniquely yours, and it did not write simply “flock.” And [as for] “your ox” — even though it could have written “with the firstborn of an ox,” and a human firstborn would also be excluded from it — even so, on account of “your flock,” it wrote “your ox.”

Rashi on Bekhorot 9b:18:3.hebrew: ה"ג - היינו דכתיב צאנך ושורך אטו צאנך, אלא לר"ש לכתוב שור וצאן:
Rashi on Bekhorot 9b:18:3.english: This is the text we read - This is [the reason] that “your flock” is written, and “your ox” [is written] on account of “your flock”; but according to Rabbi Shimon, let it write “ox and flock.”

Rashi on Bekhorot 9b:19:2.english: After breaking the neck - If he did not redeem it and broke its neck in accordance with its law.

Rashi on Bekhorot 9b:19:3.english: Forbidden - To feed it to his dog.

Rashi on Bekhorot 9b:1:1.hebrew: לימא קסברי רבנן מקצת רחם - הנוגע בבכור מקדשו. דנהי דאי אפשר לצמצם וראשון לחודיה קדיש — איכא למיפרך: הא קודם שיצא כולו, יצא אחיו וחצץ בינו לבין הרחם, וכתיב (במדבר ח׳:ט״ז): "פטר כל רחם" — עד שיפטור כל הרחם. ולר' יוסי ליכא למיפרך, דכיון דתרווייהו קדשו — כחד דמו:
Rashi on Bekhorot 9b:1:1.english: Let us say the Rabbis hold [that] a portion of the womb - [That the portion] touching the firstborn sanctifies it. For granted that it is impossible [for births] to coincide precisely, and the first one alone is sanctified, one can object: Behold, before it emerged entirely, its brother emerged and interposed between it and the womb, and it is written: “Whatever opens every womb” (Numbers 8:16) — [it is not sanctified] until it opens the entire womb. And according to Rabbi Yosei, one cannot object [this], for since both of them are sanctified, they are considered as one.

Rashi on Bekhorot 9b:21:1.hebrew: עגלה ערופה - אסורה בהנאה, משום דכתיב (דברים כא): "שם" — שם תהא קבורתה:
Rashi on Bekhorot 9b:21:1.english: A heifer whose neck is broken - It is forbidden to derive benefit [from it], as it is written (Deuteronomy 21): “There” — there shall be its burial.

Rashi on Bekhorot 9b:21:2.hebrew: ושור הנסקל - ששחטו לאחר שנגמר דינו, דלא ירדה בו טומאת נבילות. ועגלה ערופה, ששחטה לאחר ירידתה לנחל איתן, דקי"ל דהיא אוסרתה:
Rashi on Bekhorot 9b:21:2.english: And an ox that is stoned - Where one slaughtered it after its verdict was finalized, so that the impurity of a carcass did not descend upon it. And [regarding] a heifer whose neck was to be broken, where one slaughtered it after its descent to a rugged ravine, as we hold that it [the descent] renders it forbidden.

Rashi on Bekhorot 9b:21:3.english: The birds of a leper - They are forbidden from benefit, in Tractate Kiddushin (57a).

Rashi on Bekhorot 9b:21:4.hebrew: ופטר חמור - ששחטו ועדיין מפרכס, שלא ירד לטומאת נבילה; אבל אם נגע בו שרץ, מטמא טומאת אוכלים — שאם חזר ונגע באוכלים אחרים, מטמאים, אע"פ שמפרכס. דאמר בהעור והרוטב (חולין קיז:): השוחט בהמה טמאה לעובד כוכבים ומפרכסת, מטמאה טומאת אוכלים, דמהניא לה שחיטת ישראל למהוי מחשבה, הואיל ושחיטה דכוותה חזיא לה בבהמה טהורה. אי נמי, אפילו ערפו ממש, דנבילה היא, ואיכא למימר בהם טומאת אוכלים כגון דאיכא פחות מכזית מינייהו, דלא חזי לטומאת נבילות — מיצטרף בהדי פחות מכביצה אוכלין ומשלימו לכביצה:
Rashi on Bekhorot 9b:21:4.english: And a firstborn donkey - [In a case] where he slaughtered it and it is still convulsing, so that it has not [yet] descended to [the status of] the defilement of a carcass; but if a creeping creature touched it, it becomes defiled with the defilement of food — so that if it then touched other foods, they become defiled, even though it is still convulsing. As [the Gemara] says in [the chapter entitled] HaOhr VehaRotev (Chullin 117b): "One who slaughters a non-kosher animal for a gentile and it is convulsing, it becomes defiled with the defilement of food, because the slaughter by an Israelite is effective to constitute designation [as food], since a slaughter like it is effective for a kosher animal." Alternatively, even [if] he actually broke its neck, so that it is a carcass, and [the case where] one can speak of the defilement of food regarding them is, for instance, where there is less than an olive-bulk of it, which is not suitable for the defilement of carcasses, [so] it combines with less than an egg-bulk of food and completes it to an egg-bulk.

Rashi on Bekhorot 9b:21:5.hebrew: כולן מטמאין טומאת אוכלין - אם נגע בהו טומאה, ואע"ג דאינהו גופייהו אסירי, מהניא להו להכי — שאם נגעו באוכלין אחרים, מטמאין אותן:
Rashi on Bekhorot 9b:21:5.english: All of them contract the ritual impurity of food - If impurity touched them, and even though they themselves are forbidden, [this] is effective for them in this respect: that if they touch other foods, they defile them.

Rashi on Bekhorot 9b:22:1.english: All of them do not transmit impurity - Since they are forbidden from [deriving] benefit.

Rashi on Bekhorot 9b:22:2.english: A period of susceptibility - Before cooking.

Rashi on Bekhorot 9b:23:1.hebrew: לאחרים - לעובדי כוכבים, דאינו אסור בהנאה:
Rashi on Bekhorot 9b:23:1.english: To others: To idolaters, as [the food] is not forbidden from [deriving] benefit.

Rashi on Bekhorot 9b:2:1.english: A substance with the same type of substance - And both of these [fetuses] are of one kind.

Rashi on Bekhorot 9b:5:1.english: And is permitted - Prior to its redemption.

Rashi on Bekhorot 9b:5:2.hebrew: בכור אדם - מותר בהנאה למעשה ידיו קודם פדייה, דהא לא אשכחן דאסור:
Rashi on Bekhorot 9b:5:2.english: A firstborn of man - [He] is permitted for benefit with respect to the work of his hands prior to redemption, for we have not found that [he] is forbidden.

Rashi on Bekhorot 9b:5:3.hebrew: שהקפידה וכו' - וכיון דמחמיר כולי האי, שקבע לו הכתוב פדיון בשה ולא באחר, ודאי אסור בהנאה:
Rashi on Bekhorot 9b:5:3.english: About which [the Torah] was particular, etc. - And since [the Torah] is so stringent, that Scripture established for it redemption with a lamb and not with another [animal], it is certainly forbidden to derive benefit [from it].

Rashi on Bekhorot 9b:6:2.english: At its value - That he gives herbs equal to the monetary value of the donkey to the priest.

Rashi on Bekhorot 9b:6:3.hebrew: בשויו לא אמרי' - דלא חמיר מהקדשות:
Rashi on Bekhorot 9b:6:3.english: At its value, we do not say - For it is not more stringent than consecrated property.

Rashi on Bekhorot 9b:6:4.hebrew: לאפקועי לאיסורא בשה - ואפילו שלא בשויו, כדקתני מתני': "גדול וקטן":
Rashi on Bekhorot 9b:6:4.english: To abrogate its forbidden status with a lamb - And even not at its value, as the Mishnah teaches: "[Whether] large or small."

Rashi on Bekhorot 9b:7:1.hebrew: בכסף צורי - דאינו מתחלל על אסימון, כדכתיב: (דברים י״ד:כ״ה) "וצרת הכסף בידך":
Rashi on Bekhorot 9b:7:1.english: With a minted coin - For it is not deconsecrated onto an unminted token, as it is written: (Deuteronomy 14:25) “And you shall bind up the money in your hand.”

Rashi on Bekhorot 9b:7:2.english: Intentionally - That he intended to desacralize it.

Rashi on Bekhorot 9b:7:3.hebrew: קידש - אם קידש בו את האשה, מקודשת. אלמא, מותר בהנאה לר' יהודה:
Rashi on Bekhorot 9b:7:3.english: He has betrothed - If he betrothed a woman with it, she is betrothed. Consequently, it is permitted to derive benefit [from it] according to Rabbi Yehuda.

Rashi on Bekhorot 9b:9:1.english: With that which is in between - That the donkey is worth more than the lamb.

Tosafot on Bekhorot 9b:23:1.hebrew: מכל האוכל אשר יאכל אוכל שיכול להאכילו לאחרים קרוי אוכל - וא"ת: פרק כסוי הדם (חולין פה.) פטרינן עוף טמא מכסוי לרבי שמעון גבי שחיטה שאינה ראויה, מדכתיב: "ציד חיה או עוף אשר יאכל" וגו' — והא אוכל שאתה יכול להאכיל לאחרים הוא?! יש לומר: התם "חיה או עוף" כתיב — משמע דאתא למעוטי מינים טמאים שאין נאכלין לישראל, ואף על גב שיכול להאכילן לאחרים; אבל הכא "מכל האוכל אשר יאכל" — משמע שפיר למעוטי שאין נאכל לאחרים:
Tosafot on Bekhorot 9b:23:1.english: “From all food that may be eaten: Food that one is able to feed to others is called food” - And if you say: In the chapter [entitled] Kisuy HaDam (Chullin 85a), we exempt an impure bird from covering [the blood] according to Rabbi Shimon in the case of slaughter that is not fit [for consumption], because it is written: “[...who takes in hunting] any beast or fowl that may be eaten...” (Leviticus 17:13) — and isn’t it food that you are able to feed to others? One can say: There, “beast or fowl” is written, which implies that it comes to exclude impure species that are not eaten by an Israelite, even though one is able to feed them to others; but here, “from all food that may be eaten” well implies excluding [only food] that is not eaten by others [either].

Tosafot on Bekhorot 9b:2:1.hebrew: אמר רב (אשי) מין במינו אינו חוצץ - תימה: בפ' בהמה המקשה (חולין ע.) בעי: כרכתו אחותו והוציאתו, מהו? י"ל: הכא, מקצת פנוי, איכא למימר טפי "במינו אינו חוצץ"; אי נמי, אחותו הויא אינו מינו טפי מאחיו. עוד יש לומר: דוקא משום דהוציאתו, שסייעה אחותו בהוצאתו, הוא דמספקא לן דדילמא הויא חציצה; אבל אם לא סייעה להוציאו, פשיטא דלא הויא חציצה. וא"ת: [לאביי] דמוקי מתני' כר' יוסי הגלילי, דאפשר לצמצם, ואפ"ה אינו נותן כי אם טלה אחד לכהן, משום דכתיב "הזכרים" — אמאי לא אמר: "כל שאינו בזה אחר זה, בבת אחת אינו", ולא קדוש לא זה ולא זה? וי"ל: דלא מסתבר למימר הכי אלא בדבר התלוי במעשה, כההוא דקדש שתי אחיות ותודה שנשחטה על שמונים חלות; אבל קדושה הבאה מאליה לא אמר הכי, ואע"ג דשייך למימר: "הי מינייהו מייתית, הי מינייהו מפקת". ואם תאמר: מדקאמר "נהי דא"א לצמצם, חציצה מיהא איכא", משמע דה"ק: נהי דא"א לצמצם, ודין הוא שיקדש האחד לרבנן, חציצה מיהא איכא ולא היה לו להיות קדוש — משמע דאי הוה אפשר לצמצם, היה אז קשה לן היאך קדוש בלא טעם חציצה. ומה קשה? והא (פריך) [פרישית] דלא אמר "כל שאינו [כו'] בבת אחת כו'" אלא בדבר התלוי בדבור! וי"ל: דה"פ: נהי דא"א לצמצם, ולהכי ניחא לרבנן שאין שתיהן קדושין מטעם "הזכרים" כמו לרבי יוסי הגלילי, דלא אפשר למידרש להו "הזכרים" כיון דסבירא להו אי אפשר — מכל מקום ליהוי חציצה:
Tosafot on Bekhorot 9b:2:1.english: Rav (Ashi) says: A substance [in contact] with its own kind does not interpose - It is astounding: In the chapter [entitled] "Behemah HaMaksheh" (Chullin 70a), [the Gemara] raises the dilemma: If its sister wrapped around it and brought it out, what is [the halakha]? One can say: Here, [since] a portion [of the womb] is clear, it is more applicable to say [that a substance] with its own kind does not interpose; alternatively, its sister is considered "not its own kind" more than a brother. Furthermore, one can say: It was specifically because "she brought it out" — that its sister assisted in bringing it out — that we are in doubt whether perhaps it constitutes an interposition; but if she did not assist in bringing it out, it is obvious that it would not constitute an interposition. And if you say: According to [Abaye], who establishes our Mishnah in accordance with Rabbi Yosei HaGelili, [holding] that it is possible [for two births] to coincide precisely, and even so [the owner] gives only one lamb to the priest because it is written "the males" — why did he not say: "Anything that cannot [take effect] sequentially cannot [take effect] simultaneously," and neither this one nor that one should be sanctified? And one can say: It is not reasonable to say this except regarding a matter that depends on an action, like that case where one betrothed two sisters, or a thanksgiving offering that was slaughtered over eighty loaves; but regarding sanctity that comes on its own, he does not say this, even though it would be applicable to say: "Which of them will you include, [and] which of them will you exclude?" And if you say: From that which [the Gemara] says, "Granted that it is impossible to coincide precisely, in any event there is an interposition," this implies that this is what it means: Granted that it is impossible to coincide precisely, and [therefore] by rights one [of them] should be sanctified according to the Rabbis, in any event there is an interposition and it should not have been sanctified — which implies that if it were possible to coincide precisely, it would then have been difficult for us how it could be sanctified even without the reason of interposition! But why would it be difficult, seeing that [I] explained that one does not say "anything that is not [sequential is not simultaneous]" except regarding a matter that depends on speech? And one can say: This is what it means: Granted that it is impossible to coincide precisely, and for this reason it is understandable according to the Rabbis that both of them are not sanctified on account of [the verse] "the males," as [they are] according to Rabbi Yosei HaGelili — since it is impossible to expound "the males" for them, given that they hold [simultaneous emergence] is impossible — nevertheless, let there be an interposition!

Tosafot on Bekhorot 9b:3:1.hebrew: לאפקועי לאיסורא מיניה - דלפוטרו ממצות עריפה לא היה צריך להפריש מספק; כמו שאין נותן לכהן מספק, כמו כן אינו עורפו מספק:
Tosafot on Bekhorot 9b:3:1.english: In order to abrogate its forbidden status - For to exempt it from the mitzvah of breaking the neck, he would not have needed to designate [a lamb] out of uncertainty; just as he does not give [it] to the priest out of uncertainty, so too he does not break its neck out of uncertainty.

Tosafot on Bekhorot 9b:7:1.hebrew: ותנן רבי יהודה אומר במזיד קידש - משמע הכא דמקודשת בגבולין קודם שיגיע לירושלים. והא דאמר בסוף פ' חלק (סנהדרין קיב:): "בגבולין דברי הכל פטורין מן החלה" — לאו משום דחשיב ממון גבוה לכולי עלמא בגבולין, אלא משום דלא קרינן ביה "עריסותיכם", כיון דאסור באכילה; וכן עיר הנדחת לאו "שללה" הוא, כדאמר התם. בהשוכר את הפועלים (ב"מ צ.) נמי פטר ר"י מחסימה מעשר חוץ לחומה — לאו משום דחשיב ממון גבוה חוץ לחומה, אלא משום דבעינן דישוי הראוי לו, כדממעטינן הקדש ממעילה:
Tosafot on Bekhorot 9b:7:1.english: "And we learned: Rabbi Yehuda says: If intentionally, he has betrothed [her]" - It is implied here that she is betrothed [even] in the outlying areas, before [the produce] reaches Jerusalem. And as for that which [the Gemara] says at the end of the chapter [entitled] Chelek (Sanhedrin 112b): "In the outlying areas, all agree that [second-tithe dough] is exempt from challah" — [this is] not because it is considered property of Heaven according to everyone in the outlying areas, but because we do not apply to it [the verse] "your dough," since it is forbidden to be eaten [there]; and likewise, [regarding] an idolatrous city, it is not [considered] "its spoil," as [the Gemara] says there. In [the chapter entitled] Hasokher Et Hapo'alim (Bava Metzia 90a) as well, Rabbi Yehuda exempted [one who threshes with] second tithe outside the wall from [the prohibition against] muzzling — not because he considers it property of Heaven outside the wall, but because we require threshing of [produce that is] fit for it [to eat], just as we exclude consecrated property in [tractate] Me'ilah:
